title: Order Events: Requests, Ownership, and Delivery
subtitle: Arrows indicate layer grouping only. Node text defines specific dependencies, event routes, and data ownership.

nodes.name: Storefront
nodes.desc: Synchronously calls the order service to create an order.

nodes.name: Payment Platform
nodes.desc: Synchronously calls the callback service with a callback ID.

nodes.name: Order State and Event Publishing
nodes.desc: Order service: writes Order DB; publishes OrderCreated asynchronously; consumes PaymentConfirmed, committing payment status and consumed event ID together.

nodes.name: Callback Deduplication and Events
nodes.desc: Callback service: writes Callback DB; acknowledges after commit; deduplicates by callback ID; publishes PaymentConfirmed asynchronously.

nodes.name: Inventory Reservation and Deduplication
nodes.desc: Inventory consumer: receives OrderCreated asynchronously; commits reservation and consumed event ID together.

nodes.name: Order DB
nodes.desc: PostgreSQL; only the order service reads and writes it. Order and outbox commit together; stores consumed event IDs.

nodes.name: Callback DB
nodes.desc: Separate PostgreSQL; only the callback service reads and writes it. Callback ID and outbox commit together.

nodes.name: Inventory DB
nodes.desc: Separate PostgreSQL; only the inventory consumer reads and writes it. Stores reservations and consumed event IDs.

nodes.name: Business Event Queue
nodes.desc: At-least-once delivery. OrderCreated → inventory consumer; PaymentConfirmed → order service.

footer: Order and callback services retry failed publishing from their own outboxes. Callback IDs deduplicate callbacks; event IDs deduplicate order and inventory consumption. At-least-once delivery is not an exactly-once processing guarantee. Arrows are not node wiring or a serial call chain.
